body:
## What to build

Accept ordinary data.table inputs when `expand_with_margins()` is asked for Margin order. Expansion should produce the requested grouping-set rows, order their grouping keys correctly, and leave the caller's table unchanged.

## Reproduction and observed behavior

Confirmed on unmodified [6a5f611](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/commit/6a5f611d41bd462f3c933edea1dd0b9861d6e892), installed in an isolated library and exercised without testthat. R 4.6.1, dplyr 1.2.1, data.table 1.18.6.1, dtplyr 1.3.3, vctrs 0.7.3.

1. Create a one-row, one-column data.table whose character column `g` contains `"a"`.
2. Call `expand_with_margins()` with `.grouping = rollup(g)` and `.sort = "last"`; leave all other arguments at their defaults.

Expected: two rows with `g = c("a", "Total")`.

Actual: the call fails before returning a result. The error begins `When i is a data.table (or character vector), the columns to join by must be specified ...`; its call is the data.table subset method applied to `result` and `columns`.

The same failure occurs with `.sort = "first"`. Fixed keys, `.id`, missing values, factors, structured columns, and downstream verbs are not required.

Controls on the same data:

- `.sort = "none"` succeeds.
- Converting the input to a plain data.frame or an immutable dtplyr input makes ordered expansion succeed.
- The corresponding ordinary dplyr union/mutate/arrange operations succeed.
- Summary and both nesting Margin verbs accept this data.table with Margin order.
- The source table is unchanged.

A second investigator independently reproduced first/last rejection with a different two-row table, confirmed each control, and checked source preservation by serialization.

## Contract, diagnosis, and history

The [expansion contract](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/6a5f611d41bd462f3c933edea1dd0b9861d6e892/R/expand_with_margins.R) admits data-frame-compatible inputs and inherits Margin order. [ADR 0016](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/6a5f611d41bd462f3c933edea1dd0b9861d6e892/design/adr/0016-delegate-result-class-and-attributes-to-dplyr.md) delegates result class behavior to dplyr; it does not exclude data.table input or require input-class restoration.

The immediate cause is the [structured sort-column inspection](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/6a5f611d41bd462f3c933edea1dd0b9861d6e892/R/margin-operation.R), `margin_structured_sort_columns()`. It admits data.table via `is.data.frame()` and then performs one-index data.frame-style column selection. data.table interprets that operation as a row join. Even an ordinary character key passes through this inspection.

The defect also reproduces with the same dependencies at `d4ea5f09d5698a6a89b68ecfd62ad450a4089bba` and `ad851dbefe99cf1cf6987dc5f0716f6a13d3873b`, before the recent five fixes and before #640. Its first introduction was not established; do not attribute it to #651–#655.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ordered expansion of a one-row character-key data.table succeeds for both first and last Margin order, with the independently expected values and row count.
- [ ] Cover an ordinary multi-column input with fixed keys, a Grouping set identifier, and missing grouping values; preserve public columns, grouping semantics, and the documented ordering boundary.
- [ ] Leave the caller's data.table unchanged. Retain successful unordered expansion and the corresponding plain data.frame/immutable dtplyr controls.
- [ ] Preserve structured-key sorting and the documented delegation of result class/attributes. Do not turn this into a new input-class preservation promise.
- [ ] Add public-API regression tests and run the required package checks.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).
